title: Microsoft Purview: Azure PST Import to Exchange Online mailboxes
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's supplied notice, and the Azure role-assignment path, command, licensing and storage meters are supported. One checklist item asks readers to check mailbox licensing and archive enablement without corresponding controls-table rows.

claims.claim: Azure PST Import is a planned method to import PST files directly from Azure Blob Storage into Exchange Online mailboxes.
claims.quote: Azure PST Import is a migration method that enables PST files stored in Azure Blob Storage to be imported directly into Exchange Online mailboxes.

claims.claim: The standard two-step Exchange Migration Service pattern begins with analysis to validate and assess PST data.
claims.quote: It follows the standard two‑step Exchange Migration Service pattern: an initial analysis phase to validate and assess PST data, followed by execution of the actual migration.

claims.claim: The actual migration follows the initial analysis phase.
claims.quote: an initial analysis phase to validate and assess PST data, followed by execution of the actual migration.

claims.claim: The existing Microsoft Purview portal PST import supports network upload.
claims.quote: Network upload: Upload the PST files over the network to a temporary Azure Storage location in the Microsoft cloud.

claims.claim: The existing Microsoft Purview portal PST import also supports drive shipping.
claims.quote: Drive shipping: Copy the PST files to a BitLocker-encrypted hard drive and then physically ship the drive to Microsoft.

claims.claim: For the existing portal process, administrators create an import job on the Import PST files page in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Create a PST import job on the Import PST files page in the Microsoft Purview portal and submit the PST import mapping file you created in the previous step.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not name the Exchange or Purview admin roles needed to run the cmdlets.
claims.quote: The feature is controlled through administrator access to PowerShell cmdlets and Azure role assignments, including permissions on the Azure storage account used for PST import.

claims.claim: In Azure portal, the route is storage account > Access control (IAM) > Role assignments > Add > Add role assignment > Role > Job function roles > Storage Blob Data Reader > Members > User, group, or service principal > Select members > Office 365 Import Service.
claims.quote:
Click Access control (IAM).
Click the Role assignments tab to view the role assignments at this scope.
Click Add > Add role assignment.
On the Role tab, select the tab for the type of role you want to assign.
Click Select members.

claims.claim: az role assignment create --role "Storage Blob Data Reader" --assignee-object-id "<object-id>" --assignee-principal-type "<type>" --scope "<storage-account-scope>" assigns the role to the specified principal at storage-account scope.
claims.quote:
az role assignment create \
    --role "Storage Blob Data Reader" \
    --assignee-object-id "aaaaaaaa-0000-1111-2222-bbbbbbbbbbbb" \
    --assignee-principal-type "User" \
